title: Customer-driven data suppression API and test harness
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Build a customer-facing suppression API and internal test harness that lets customers request granular suppression of console/analytics events (by customer_id, workspace_id, timeframe, and event-type). The feature must be auditable, respect legal-hold exemptions, and be safe for large backfills. Deliverables: 1) Public API endpoints and internal worker contract for suppression requests; 2) Console action + UX hook (PM/design will supply minimal UI) to submit requests; 3) A test harness that simulates suppression requests against live-ish data (staging) including backfill / stream-rewrite scenarios and measures correctness; 4) Audit trail tokens and attestation logs for compliance reporting.
acceptance_criteria: 1) API: POST /suppression-requests accepts structured requests and returns a suppression_id token within 2s for 95% of requests. 2) Enforcement: Subsequent analytics reads/exports exclude suppressed events (by id or by canonical mapping) within SLA (background job completes by configured window). 3) Legal hold: suppression requests flagged with legal_hold_exempt must be persisted and fail with 409 when a legal hold exists for the scope; non-exempt requests must be queued. 4) Backfill-safety: when suppression applies to historical shards we must emit tombstone markers and ensure downstream aggregations skip suppressed rows. 5) Auditability: every suppression action produces an immutable attestation record (suppression_id, requester, scope, timestamp, reason, wave_id) stored in audit-store. 6) Tests: harness includes deterministic scenarios (single-event, multi-shard, concurrent suppression + ingestion) and a smoke test that validates suppression_id -> event absent mapping. 7) Metrics: counter for suppression_requests, suppression_failures, average_suppression_latency, and number of events removed; dashboards wired in console-2026.03 release.
design_notes: - Use a lightweight suppression request schema: {scope_type, scope_id, event_filters[], effective_from, effective_to, reason, legal_hold_exempt:false}. - Generate a cryptographically random suppression_id and issuance token for attestation. - Persist request in suppression-control-table (immutable except for status transitions) with an append-only event stream for audit. - Workers consume requests and create tombstones in event-store and emit control messages to downstream consumers (analytics pipeline, export service). - Where possible prefer idempotent operations and include idempotency_token to avoid double-work during retries. - For large scopes (whole workspaces), employ phased wave deletes: wave size configurable per request; worker writes wave manifests for progress tracking and retries. - Provide visibility endpoints: GET /suppression-requests/{id} returns status, current_progress, wave_manifest_urls. - Test harness will include a synthetic event generator, a replay controller that can inject out-of-order events, and an assertion engine that compares pre/post ingestion query fingerprints.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (API + persistence): define schema, implement POST/GET endpoints, persist request and emit event to suppression-stream. Phase 2 (worker + tombstones): implement worker that reads suppression-stream, writes tombstones to event-store and signals downstream. Phase 3 (harness + tests): deliver test harness, build e2e scenarios, add dashboards and alerts. Phase 4 (rollout): enable feature behind feature-flag, run with small internal customer, then gradated rollouts to larger customers. Rollback plan: suppression writes are reversible only by replaying original data from immutable source (rare) — we will provide a manual restore process via support runbook.
rollout_strategy: - Start feature-flagged in staging with synthetic dataset (test harness). - Canary: enable for internal orgs + one low-traffic customer for 2 weeks. Monitor suppression failures and audit integrity. - Gradual ramp: enable for 10% of customers, then 50%, then GA. - Hard gates: zero critical audit mismatches, suppression failure rate <0.5% for 48h, and no increased export discrepancy incidents.
monitoring_and_metrics: Emit metrics to telemetry: suppression.request.count, suppression.request.latency_ms, suppression.worker.errors, suppression.wave.duration, suppression.events_removed. Add alert: suppression.worker.errors > 1% over 5m. Dashboard: per-customer progress, stuck-wave table (waves older than N hours), recently failed suppression requests. Audit drift detector: periodic job comparing sample of pre-suppression exports to post-suppression exports (expect removed rows only).
privacy_and_compliance_considerations: - All suppression requests are treated as PII-affecting operations and require an audit attestation. - Use KMS-wrapped tokens for suppression_id issuance. - Ensure suppression metadata stored in audit-store is retained per legal retention policy; actual suppressed content must be erased according to retention rule. - Legal hold checks must consult legal-hold-index (read-only) before executing destructive waves. - Security review required before GA; threat model includes unauthorized suppression issuance and illicit restores.
risks_and_mitigations: 1) Risk: Large workspace suppression can take long and impact pipeline throughput. Mitigation: phased waves, backpressure-aware workers, and priority queue for small requests. 2) Risk: Missed tombstones due to race with ingestion. Mitigation: worker idempotency, idempotency tokens on tombstone writes, and a reconciliation job that re-scans recent ingestion windows. 3) Risk: Audit mismatch causing compliance exposure. Mitigation: end-to-end attestation tokens, signed wave manifests, and pre-rollout audit smoke tests.
acceptance_test_plan: - Unit tests for API schema validation and permission checks. - Integration tests for persistence, suppression-stream emission, and tombstone writes (using test harness). - e2e scenario: create workspace with known events, issue suppression for subset, run worker, assert events absent in exports and presence of audit attestation. - Fuzz: concurrent suppression + ingestion to ensure determinism. - Performance: submit synthetic large suppression (simulated 10M events) in staging to validate wave handling.
next_steps: 1) Finalize API schema with PM/design (blocker: waiting on design microcopy). 2) Kick off PR for suppression-control-table schema (ENG-612345 owns infra schema migration). 3) Prepare test harness infra on staging cluster (owner: QA infra). 4) Schedule security review for 2026-03-01 (owner: security).
